Certified type:
- Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — the schema examples say "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system"... This is a Non-automatic weighing instrument (NAWIs are under R76). I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- Type designations: RLS1000, RLS1100, RLS1000A, RLS1100A, RLS1000B, RLS1100B, RLS1000C, RLS1100C, RLS1000D, RLS1100D
- Module designation: hmm — for R76 modular approach, the certificate mentions load cell and indicator modules. The schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. This is a complete instrument cert, so maybe "Not applicable" or null. The cert covers the complete instrument. I'll leave null or "Not applicable". Actually the characteristics table describes the complete weighing instrument. I'll put null... Actually the certified type is a complete instrument; the module designation concept applies to module certificates. I'll use null.

Model family: The cert covers multiple type designations (RLS1000, RLS1100, and variants A–D). The characteristics don't vary per model in the table — Max is 6–30 kg for all. Should I create a model_family? Rule 4 says include only if cert covers >1 model variant. There are 10 type designations. But no attribute varies per model. I could include model_family with models list, but characteristics model_level would be empty. Hmm. The type designations are listed; maybe include model_family with the models but no varying attributes. I think it's reasonable to include the family models list. But it might be noise. The rule: "model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". It covers 10 designations. I'll include them as models with no attributes (or maybe attributes noting weighing ranges?). Actually the models differ by suffix A–D which likely indicate different configurations, but the cert doesn't say what varies. I'll include the models list without attributes.

Components: The test reports mention load cell ZEMIC L6D and indicator RLS1000. These are named sub-assemblies (modules). Rule 6: components for complex instruments. Include:
- role: "load cell", type_designations: ["L6D"], manufacturer: Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instrument Co., Ltd. (ZEMIC). The schema doesn't have manufacturer field for components, but characteristics can hold sub-characteristics. I could add a "manufacturer" field — schema says components[]: role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. Stick to schema; maybe put manufacturer in characteristics? Not required. I'll keep to schema fields. Actually adding a manufacturer field may violate schema adherence. The schema shows only those fields; I'll keep role and type_designations, maybe characteristics with accuracy class III. Hmm, load cell class not stated. Keep simple.

- role: "indicator", type_designations: ["RLS1000"] (also RLS1100 presumably, but only RLS1000 is mentioned in the test report). I'll record as stated.

Characteristics type_level:
- accuracy_class: (III) → value "III"? The accuracy class is also in recommendation.accuracy_classes. For characteristics, maybe accuracy_class: {value: "III"}. The table says "Accuracy class (III)". I'll include as string "III".
- maximum_capacity: 6 kg ≤ Max ≤ 30 kg → value {min: 6, max: 30}, unit kg.
- verification_scale_interval: e ≥ 2 g → value {min: 2, max: null}, unit g.
- weighing_ranges: Single interval / Multi-interval → string list? Value could be ["Single interval", "Multi-interval"]? The structured value says value: number | {min,max} | string. Hmm, two options. I could emit as two config_level entries with axis "weighing_range_type": single vs multi. Actually the table distinguishes:
  - Max number of scale intervals (one weighing range): n ≤ 3000 divisions
  - Max number of scale intervals (multi-interval): n ≤ 3000 divisions (per partial weighing range)
  - Max number of partial weighing ranges: 2
  - Tare: T ≤ -50% for single; T ≤ -Max₁ for multi-interval

This suggests config_level with axis "weighing_range_configuration" values "single_interval" and "multi_interval".

config_level entries:
- attribute: max_scale_intervals, axis: weighing_range_configuration, values: [{condition: "single_interval (one weighing range)", value: {max: 3000}, unit_symbol: "divisions"}, {condition: "multi_interval (per partial weighing range)", value: {max: 3000}, unit_symbol: "divisions"}]

Wait, value structure: for config_level, "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". So value inside can be {min,max}.

- attribute: max_partial_weighing_ranges: value 2 (type_level, dimensionless).
- attribute: tare_limit, axis: weighing_range_configuration:
  - single: T ≤ -50% → value {max: -50}, unit "%" — reference Max? "T ≤ -50%" meaning tare ≤ -50% of Max? Keep as {max: -50}, unit "%".
  - multi: T ≤ -Max₁ → string value "-Max1"? Formula → keep as string: value "-Max1", unit null. Hmm. I'd record {condition: "multi_interval", value: "≤ -Max₁"}? Better: value "-Max1", unit null, maybe note. Keep string "-Max1".

- temperature_range: 0 °C / +40 °C → {min: 0, max: 40}, unit °C.
- power_supply_voltage: 110–240 V → {min:110, max:240}, V.
- power_supply_type: AC.
- power_supply_frequency: 50/60 Hz → {min:50, max:60}, Hz.
- application: "Intended to be used for direct sales to the public" → string value. Label: direct_sales_use? attribute "application": value string. Maybe attribute "intended_use". I'll use application.
- software_identification: version V1.xxx (x = 0...999) and checksum D735A750. Split:
  - software_version: "V1.xxx" string.
  - software_checksum: "D735A750".

Recommendation:
- id: R76 (canonical), edition: 2006, scheme: A, accuracy_classes: ["III"].

Note: the certificate number prefix "R76/2006" — edition 2006. amendment: null.

- NMi-10200947-08, dated 24 December 2010, 59 pages, role: test_report.
- NMi-16200832-01, dated 6 March 2017, 21 pages, role: test_report (for indicator).
- NMi-15200788-01, dated 14 November 2016, 62 pages, role: type_evaluation_report (for complete instrument). These are all OIML Test Reports; the complete one is the type evaluation report. I'd mark the complete instrument one as "type_evaluation_report" and the module ones as "test_report". Dates: convert to ISO? Schema says date; use "2010-12-24" or keep as-is. I'll use ISO dates.

Revision history: none. Footnotes: none.

Matrix tables: none needed (the characteristics table is key-value, captured in characteristics).

Model family: include with models list of the 10 designations. Should I? The rule says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. It does — 10 variants. Attributes don't vary. I'll include models with model_id only.

Family name: null (no explicit family name). Could argue "RLS1000/RLS1100 series" but not stated; null.

certificate.page_total: 2.

Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument". The schema example list includes "Measuring system", etc. NAWI fits.

Also description: "A Non-automatic weighing instrument" — could put in description. I'll include description: "Non-automatic weighing instrument intended to be used for direct sales to the public". Actually the identification says "A Non-automatic weighing instrument". I'll set description accordingly.

Module designation: The cert covers the complete instrument, and modules (load cell + indicator). The schema's module_designation examples: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. For a complete instrument cert, "Not applicable" seems right. I'll use "Not applicable".

Wait — but the components: should I include the load cell and indicator? The certificate names them in the test reports section: "For the load cell: ZEMIC type L6D", "For the indicator: Xiamen Rongta type RLS1000". Rule 6 says record named sub-assemblies. Yes, include components.

Also compatibility: "the compatibility of load cells and indicator is established by the manufacturer by means of the compatibility of modules form, contained in OIML R76 edition 2006 Annex F." Could be noted in... maybe not needed. Could add to certified_type.description. I'll leave it out or add to description. Hmm, keep description concise.

Date issued: "15 March 2018" → "2018-03-15".

Let me double check tare: "T ≤ -50% for instruments with one weighing range" — negative tare. unit "%" and reference Max? I'll add unit_symbol "%". For multi: "T ≤ -Max₁" — value string "-Max1", unit null. Subscript ₁ — avoid LaTeX but unicode subscript is okay? Rules say no LaTeX; unicode subscript should be fine but let me write "Max1". Keep "≤ -Max1"? The value shape should not include operators ideally... but it's a limit expression. I'll use value: "-Max1" string. Hmm, maybe "Max1" with negative implied... I'll use "-Max1".

Accuracy class in characteristics: value "III" string.

Maximum number of scale intervals: value {min: null, max: 3000}, unit "divisions".

Verification scale interval: {min: 2, max: null}, unit "g".

Maximum capacity: {min: 6, max: 30}, unit "kg".

Temperature: {min: 0, max: 40}, unit "°C".

Voltage: {min: 110, max: 240}, "V".

Frequency: {min: 50, max: 60}, "Hz".

Software version: "V1.xxx" — could also record "V1.000–V1.999"? Keep "V1.xxx".

Now the config_level structure per schema: config_level[]: attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}. But rule 5 says values follow {condition, value, unit_symbol}. I'll include unit_symbol per value.

For max_scale_intervals config: single → {max: 3000} divisions; multi → {max: 3000} divisions with condition note "per partial weighing range".
